newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's CGT union mulls Nov 20 general strike.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's CGT union mulls Nov 20 general strike.

text.p: Argentina's largest union confederation is considering a 36-hour walkout on November 20, the third general strike in four months, to protest proposed labor reforms, a union spokesman said Monday.
The spokesman said leaders of the Confederacion General del Trabajo (CGT) will decide this week in meetings whether to agree to the walkout sought by several union sectors.
The CGT, whose unions represent nine million workers, about a quarter of Argentina's population, held a 24-hour general strike in August and a 36-hour stoppage in September.

The CGT was long the backbone of the governing Peronist Party. But it has clashed with President Carlos Menem this year over worker benefit cuts, tax hikes and plans to reform labor laws and end the unions' virtual monopoly on healthcare.

Menem says scrapping collective wage deals and swapping redundancy payouts for unemployment insurance is the best way to combat the high joblessness rate, now at 17.1 percent against seven percent when the president first took office in 1989.

Menem, striving to bridge an expected $6 billion fiscal gap this year, has threatened to push this through Congress by decree. Unions have influence with many Peronist deputies, without whose support it could be difficult to pass the bills.
The government also plans to allow workers to choose from any union health plan as of next January, and, in a second stage, make unions plans compete with private medical funds.
Officials say deregulation would improve service in the $2.5-billion-a-year health system. Many union plans are deep in debt and many members have additional private coverage.
But the CGT argues union health plans are the only ones that can ensure coverage to all workers regardless of income.
